newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Observers say Nicaragua elections legitimate.
newsitem.headline: Observers say Nicaragua elections legitimate.

text.p: Observers monitoring Nicaragua's presidential election from the Organisation of American States (OAS) and the European Union (EU) said on Sunday night that the vote had been legitimate despite some delays and administrative glitches.

"The mission of OAS observers has at no time found any desire to twist the will of the people of Nicaragua or any attempt at fraud," OAS Secretary General Cesar Gaviria told a news conference in the capital Managua after polls closed.
Gaviria, a former president of Colombia, added that the election results would be "legitimate" and called on all Nicaraguans to accept them when they were announced.
"Despite the problems, the day is ending with the free expression of the people," he said.
European Union observers also said Nicaragua's election day was marked by calm and they saw no serious difficulties.

They said the chief problems were election materials not delivered in time at the start of the day and some voting officials arriving late, but added that "the anomalies have been overcome in great part."

"According to preliminary information, the European Union believes that the electoral process of October 20, 1996, will contribute to the consolidation of democracy in Nicaragua and the Central American region," the EU delegation said in a statement.
Nicaragua's Supreme Electoral Council said 1,650 foreign and 4,380 Nicaraguan observers watched the October 20 vote.
